task_card.title: Gallery renditions - size-matched image thumbs and a video proxy

next_action.description: Read .agents/mpi-kanban/tasks/MPI-633/validation.md (the Phase 0 numbers) and checklist.md, then build Phase 1 + Phase 1b TOGETHER - the image rendition ladder and the image-side demote are one change, because M2 measured the ladder costing 238 MB without the demote and 23.7 MB with only the visible band resident. key_decisions: Top rendition tier stays at 1024-1280px clamped to the source. Fabio was offered a lower cap to save disk and encode time and declined: 'there's no point going lower'.

Phase 1 and Phase 1b ship together. A ladder without the demote measured 238 MB resting at the largest card size against 12 MB today - the quality fix would cost 20x VRAM. With only the visible band resident the same config costs 23.7 MB, so the demote is what makes the ladder affordable, not a nice-to-have.

Video proxy = 720p. M1 measured 1152x720 at 11-21 MB per promoted card against 65-81 for 3000x1280 (a 6x cut); 480p buys perhaps 10 MB/video more and is visibly softer on a 775px card at slider level 4.

The brief's arithmetic flatness table is WRONG and should not be trusted for any further design: it predicted ~24 vs ~22 MB across the slider, the measured pair on today's build is 34-42 (smallest cards) vs 12 (largest). Today's gallery is CHEAPER at the largest card size, because it holds fewer cards at the same 512px source.
constraints: MEASURING VRAM NEEDS A NON-E2E LAUNCH. tests/desktop/launch.js sets CUBRIC_E2E and main.js:259 turns that into disableHardwareAcceleration() + --disable-gpu, so every GPU sample reads 0.0 MB on a perfectly healthy app. The rigs launch Electron themselves without that flag while keeping CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA + the run's CUBRIC_PORT, which is what actually keeps them off the user's app.

DO NOT SAMPLE BY PROCESS TREE. Win32_Process reports NO children for the Electron main pid (measured: tree(1) while getAppMetrics listed Browser/GPU/Tab/Utility), and app.process().pid is a cmd.exe shim on Windows. The pid list must come from app.getAppMetrics(). Three rig runs read a confident 0.0 MB before this was found.

ONE APP LAUNCH PER MEASURED CONFIG. A torn-down grid does not hand GPU memory back within seconds (a 3000x1280 run left 740 MB resident after unmount), so configs sharing a process measure only what they need BEYOND the pool the previous config grew. The first ladder pass was junk for exactly this reason.

A SCROLL TOUR MUST STEP BY A VIEWPORT, not by a fraction of scrollHeight. Level 4's content is ~9x taller than level 1's, so a fixed step count skips ~60% of the cards at L4 and none at L1 - the two runs then differ in how many cards were ever rasterised rather than in what a card costs. Same family as MPI-631's fixture that overflowed by only 361px.

WebP, never JPG, for any image rendition (MPI-627): JPG has no alpha, so flattening a background-removed PNG hands back the ORIGINAL image whole, backdrop included, and the card then silently disagrees with the viewer. The symptom is NOT a white background.
Never generate a rendition larger than its source - most assets in the test project are 1280x800, so at a large card size the ORIGINAL is the right file.
extractImageThumb returns the path it ACTUALLY wrote (always .webp); callers must use the return value, not the path they passed.

The rigs are .rig.js on purpose - Playwright's testMatch only takes *.spec.js/*.test.js, so they stay out of npm run test:desktop. Do not rename them to .spec.js; each run is 3-5 minutes and launches 5-7 Electron instances. Fixture dir comes from MPI633_SCRATCH (default <tmp>/mpi633); rebuild the fixtures with tasks/MPI-633/rig/ladder.sh and rig/m2media.sh.

A stale file-claim record (ab0f51bf-095f-4c37-9c54-90f90844b263) still holds MpiGalleryGrid.js for MPI-573, which is in done, heartbeat 2026-08-22. It is not a live peer - but guard-claim may still object, and the record wants clearing rather than working around.
